claim: The migration indexes `[0]` on the embed_category query result without checking for rows; on any site that never set `embed_category` the result is empty and pg raises IndexError, aborting the migration.
body:
## [ISSUE] Migration crashes on sites that never configured `embed_category`

**Severity:** HIGH — The migration indexes `[0]` on the embed_category query result without checking for rows; on any site that never set `embed_category` the result is empty and pg raises IndexError, aborting the migration.

### The Problem
```ruby
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
                    INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
                    WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```
The `if category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 suggests the author expected a missing setting to produce `0`. It does not. The lookup fails before `.to_i` runs.

### Theory / Proof
Discourse only writes a row to `site_settings` when an admin changes a setting from its default. `embed_category` defaulted to `''` (removed from `config/site_settings.yml` in this PR), so on most installs there is no row and the INNER JOIN returns zero tuples. The same is true when the configured name no longer matches a category, for example after a rename. With pg 0.18.1 (`Gemfile.lock`), `PG::Result#[]` raises `IndexError: Index 0 is out of range` for an out-of-range tuple index. It does not return `nil`. Even if it returned `nil`, `nil['id']` would raise NoMethodError.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The migration only succeeds when `embed_category` is set to an existing category name. On every other install `rake db:migrate` fails partway. On PostgreSQL the DDL is transactional, so the table creation rolls back and the deploy/upgrade is blocked.

### Research
Rails' `select_value` returns `nil` when there are no rows, and that is how Discourse migrations normally read a single value, for example `SiteSetting` backfills using `select_value`/`select_values`.

### Recommendation
```ruby
category_id = select_value(<<~SQL).to_i
  SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
  INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
  WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'
SQL

if category_id == 0
  category_id = select_value("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'").to_i
end
```

claim: Legacy host strings are copied verbatim (no scheme/path stripping, no quoting), so entries like `http://example.com` never match `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which silently disables embedding after upgrade; a `'` in the value also breaks the SQL.
body:
## [ISSUE] Migrated hosts are not normalised, so existing embeds stop working after upgrade

**Severity:** HIGH — Legacy host strings are copied verbatim (no scheme/path stripping, no quoting), so entries like `http://example.com` never match `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which silently disables embedding after upgrade; a `'` in the value also breaks the SQL.

### The Problem
```ruby
records = val.split("\n")
records.each do |h|
  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"
end
```
Every raw line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting goes straight into `embeddable_hosts.host`.

### Theory / Proof
The old setting accepted full URLs. The removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` ran `URI(h).host || h`, and the removed specs covered `'http://eviltrout.com'`, `'https://eviltrout.com'` and `"#{host}\nhttp://discourse.org\nhttps://example.com/1234"`. The new lookup is
```ruby
where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host).first   # app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17
```
so the stored value has to be a bare hostname. The model's `before_validation` hook strips `https?://` and paths, but raw `INSERT` statements bypass ActiveRecord callbacks. A migrated row with the value `http://eviltrout.com` is therefore compared against `eviltrout.com` and never matches. Lines ending in `\r` from textarea input, and empty lines, get the same treatment. String interpolation also means a value that contains `'` breaks the statement.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Sites that entered hosts with a scheme, which the old UI and specs explicitly supported, pass migration with no error. Afterwards `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` raises `InvalidAccess('invalid referer host')` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` returns true for every embed request, so comments stop loading on every embedding site and there is no error in the logs.

### Research
The removed code, `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`, already normalised hosts at comparison time. The new model moves normalisation to write time, so data migrated into it has to be normalised the same way.

### Recommendation
Normalise and quote while migrating:
```ruby
val.split(/\r?\n/).map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?).each do |h|
  h = h.sub(/\Ahttps?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*\z/, '').downcase
  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at)
           VALUES (#{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)}, #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
end
```

claim: The host validation accepts a `:port` suffix, but `record_for_host` compares against `URI#host` (which never includes the port), so any host saved with a port is accepted by the admin UI yet can never match.
body:
## [ISSUE] Validator accepts `host:port`, but lookup can never match it

**Severity:** MEDIUM — The host validation accepts a `:port` suffix, but `record_for_host` compares against `URI#host` (which never includes the port), so any host saved with a port is accepted by the admin UI yet can never match.

### The Problem
```ruby
validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i
...
host = uri.host
where("lower(host) = ?", host).first
```
The `before_validation` hook removes the scheme and path but leaves `:8080` in place.

### Theory / Proof
Per RFC 3986 §3.2, `URI::Generic#host` returns only the reg-name and `#port` is a separate attribute. `URI('http://example.com:8080/x').host == 'example.com'`. A stored row of `example.com:8080` is therefore compared as `'example.com:8080' = 'example.com'`, which is always false.

### What happens today vs. what will break
An admin who enters `staging.example.com:8080` sees the host saved and listed as valid, but every embed from that host is rejected with `invalid referer host`. The UI implies port-specific hosts are supported when they are not.

### Research
The removed `allows_embeddable_host?` ran `URI(h).host`, which dropped the port, so `http://example.com:8080` in the old setting matched `example.com`.

### Recommendation
Pick one behaviour. Either strip the port on save:
```ruby
before_validation do
  self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')
  self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')
  self.host.sub!(/:\d+$/, '')
end
```
or remove `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` from the regex so the form rejects the value.

claim: `update`/`destroy` use `where(id:).first` and then dereference the result, and `save_host` assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` and its `:host` exist, so a stale id or a malformed request raises NoMethodError (500) instead of 404/400/422.
body:
## [ISSUE] Missing record or params produce 500s instead of 4xx

**Severity:** MEDIUM — `update`/`destroy` use `where(id:).first` and then dereference the result, and `save_host` assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` and its `:host` exist, so a stale id or a malformed request raises NoMethodError (500) instead of 404/400/422.

### The Problem
```ruby
def update
  host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first
  save_host(host)          # host may be nil -> nil.host= NoMethodError
end

def destroy
  host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first
  host.destroy             # nil.destroy -> NoMethodError
```
`save_host` also calls `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which raises if the root key is missing. If `:host` is missing, `EmbeddableHost#before_validation` calls `nil.sub!` (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6`), which also raises.

### Theory / Proof
`ActiveRecord::Relation#first` returns `nil` when nothing matches. `ApplicationController` rescues `Discourse::NotFound` and `ActionController::ParameterMissing` into 404/400 responses, but it does not handle NoMethodError, which becomes a 500 and gets logged as an exception.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The Ember UI normally sends well-formed requests. The error path is hit when two admins work at once (one deletes a host while the other edits or deletes it) or when someone calls the admin API directly. In those cases the user gets a generic 500 instead of a "not found" or validation message.

### Research
Sibling admin controllers use `find`/`find_by` together with `raise Discourse::NotFound`, for example `Admin::PermalinksController#destroy` uses `Permalink.find(params[:id])`, and they read params with `params.require`.

### Recommendation
```ruby
def update
  save_host(EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id]))
end

def destroy
  EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id]).destroy
  render json: success_json
end

def save_host(host)
  attrs = params.require(:embeddable_host)
  host.host = attrs[:host].to_s
  ...
```
Also guard the model hook with `self.host = host.to_s`, or `return if host.blank?`.

claim: The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed/false; `expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts at all, so the test asserts a behaviour that no longer exists.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] `expandable_first_post?` spec no longer tests what its name says

**Severity:** LOW — The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed/false; `expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts at all, so the test asserts a behaviour that no longer exists.

### The Problem
```ruby
it "is false if embeddable_host is blank" do
  expect(topic.expandable_first_post?).to eq(false)
end
```
The implementation is now `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (`app/models/topic.rb:869`). No EmbeddableHost is checked.

### Theory / Proof
The spec is outside the `with an emeddable host` block, so `embed_truncate` keeps its default of `false` and `has_topic_embed?` is not stubbed. The expectation holds whatever the embeddable-host state is. The PR removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard but kept a test named after it.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The test passes, but it would still pass if hosts did matter again, or if the removed guard were needed. Deleting every embeddable host no longer stops the truncated first post from being expanded, and nothing in the suite documents that change.

### Research
Test names should describe the condition under test. A test that passes for an unrelated reason gives false confidence.

### Recommendation
Either restore the check, `EmbeddableHost.exists? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, and keep the spec, or rename or remove the spec so it matches the new behaviour:
```ruby
it "is false when embed_truncate is disabled" do
  SiteSetting.embed_truncate = false
  topic.stubs(:has_topic_embed?).returns(true)
  expect(topic.expandable_first_post?).to eq(false)
end
```

claim: After saving a host with no category chosen, the client sets `host.category` to `findById(null)` (undefined) while the server stored `uncategorized_category_id`, so the row shows no category badge until reload.

The new `_ids` branch maps ids through `_lookupSubType` without filtering, so ids missing from the side-loaded collection become `undefined` array entries (the `|| []` is dead code), and templates iterating the array will crash on them.
